messages:
Priya: quick sync follow-up: how strict do we want project boundaries for SDKs used by customers? some SDKs are single-token multi-project in current clients.
Eli: For public SDKs we should default to single-project tokens; consuming multiple projects should require explicit multi-project token creation with owner approval. prevents accidental bleed.
Josef: Implementation: API accepts scope list in token create: scopes: [org:123/project:abc, org:123/project:def]. token metadata stores allowed_envs. tooling warns on cross-project scopes.
Anna L.: audit requirement: if a token is used in a project not in its scope, we should emit a high-severity alert and block the operation in strict mode. in permissive mode we log and tag for rotation.
Priya: migration: detect SDKs that store tokens in env vars in CI across multiple projects -> notify repo owners. provide helper action to rotate tokens to per-project.
Eli: CLI UX: `redwood auth token create --projects p1,p2 --expiry 30d --purpose \"ci build\"` and default to requiring interactive confirmation for multi-project.
Josef: we also need service-principal impersonation flow: `POST /v1/token/impersonate` with body {subject, delegates, lifetime} returning JWT. require caller to have impersonation capability. log delegate chain.
Anna L.: security-bot action: add detection rule for cross-project token usage and P0 alert if legacy token used to access prod from dev.
security-bot: created alert rule SEC-8020 \"Cross-project token usage detection\" assigned to oncall.
Eli: plan to include unit tests: 1) token with p1 only denied on p2 resources, 2) multi-project token allowed, 3) impersonation chain length limited to 3.
Priya: good. I'll draft SDK guidance and CLI examples. thanks everyone, will collect notes into the RFC PR.
